who: Medieval intellectual historian at Barnard College, Columbia University; PhD University of Pennsylvania.

evidence.says: Joined Barnard in 1992; specializes in medieval intellectual history, science and economic thought; holds a Pennsylvania PhD.
Identifies Joel Kaye with Barnard, a Pennsylvania PhD, and Economy and Nature in the Fourteenth Century; cites his Barnard history appointment beginning in 1992.
Lists Joel Kaye of Barnard among Columbia's history faculty.
The alternative candidate is John Marsh Kaye, using J. M. Kaye, affiliated with Queen's College, Oxford, in A God's House Miscellany.

notes: Pennsylvania doctorate, medieval field and Barnard/Columbia affiliation identify p-114414. The John Marsh Kaye candidate is a different person.

who: Andrew J. Kirkendall, Latin American historian at Texas A&M since 1997; PhD UNC-Chapel Hill 1996.

evidence.says: CV records a 1996 UNC-Chapel Hill PhD in Latin American history, Texas A&M appointments since 1997, and doctoral advisees Laurence Nelson (2023) and Micah Wright (2020).
Andrew J. Kirkendall's authority cites his 1996 UNC-Chapel Hill history dissertation on student culture in nineteenth-century Brazil and his book Class Mates.

notes: Both listed students, their completion years, and the supervisor's own doctorate match.

who: Scott Kurashige, historian of race and Asian American history at Michigan during the students' studies; UCLA history PhD 2000.

evidence.says: Michigan's tenure communication records a UCLA history doctorate in 2000 and Michigan faculty service beginning that year, with tenure in 2006.
Lists Scott Kurashige as Maria Paz Esguerra's advisor for Interracial Romances of American Empire, under 2013 graduates.
Identifies Scott Kurashige as author of The Shifting Grounds of Race and The Fifty-Year Rebellion, with scholarship on race, Asian American studies, urbanism and social movements.

notes: Direct advisor evidence and the UCLA doctorate support the match. Michigan lists Esguerra under 2013 rather than the AHA's 2014; the dissertation title also varies slightly.

who: Nancy H. Kwak, urban historian at UC San Diego since 2008; Columbia history PhD 2006.

who: Andrew F. Lang, Civil War historian at Mississippi State University; Rice history PhD 2013.

evidence.says: Describes Lang's nineteenth-century American and Civil War scholarship, lists a Rice history PhD in 2013, and includes In the Wake of War and A Contest of Civilizations.
Identifies Andrew F. Lang as author of those books and a history professor at Mississippi State.
Identifies Lucas Wilder as a Mississippi State doctoral student in Civil War and environmental history and Andrew Lang as one of his faculty mentors.
The alternative Andrew Lang authority concerns a poet, novelist, literary critic and anthropology writer, with works including The Blue Fairy Book and Myth, Ritual and Religion.

notes: The Mississippi State appointment, Rice doctorate and publications identify p-104822; p-128291 is the different literary author.

who: Malinda Maynor Lowery, historian of Indigenous history and the US South; UNC-Chapel Hill faculty 2009-2021, UNC history PhD 2005.

evidence.says: CV records a UNC-Chapel Hill history PhD in 2005 and successive UNC history appointments from July 2009 through June 2021.
Identifies Malinda Maynor Lowery as an American historian who moved to Emory in July 2021 after twelve years at UNC; lists the 2005 doctorate and her books on Lumbee history.
Identifies Malinda Maynor Lowery as author of Lumbee Indians in the Jim Crow South and The Lumbee Indians, also connecting the name to her earlier Harvard history appointment.

notes: Name, doctorate and UNC career match. Her move to Emory in 2021 precedes Dry's listed completion year; no claim of a continuing UNC faculty appointment in 2023 is made.

who: Gladys McCormick, historian of Mexico and Latin America at Syracuse; Wisconsin-Madison PhD 2009.

Syracuse's repository names Gladys McCormick as advisor of Henry John Stegeman's May 2018 history PhD dissertation on indigenismo and Mapuche politics in Chile.
Identifies Gladys I. McCormick, author of The Logic of Compromise in Mexico, as a Syracuse history professor specializing in Latin America and Mexico.

notes: Direct supervision of Stegeman, the doctorate and the candidate's publication and affiliation match.

Identifies Rebecca Tinio McKenna, author of American Imperial Pastoral, with Notre Dame's history department and research on US imperialism, political economy and culture.
Public profile supplies only the given name Rebecca, without surname, biography or researcher links.
